---
title: Files
description: How Marfa keeps a file's bytes once, however many items name them, who may read them, and how long they stay.
job: A builder learns how a file's bytes are kept once, who may read them and how long they stay.
kind: concept
---

**A file in Marfa is two things.** The bytes are a **blob**, stored once under a hash of their content. The file itself is an **item**, which names the blob by that hash and holds everything else: a title, a media type, an image's size. The same bytes uploaded twice are stored once, and an item stays small enough for every working copy to hold.

## A blob and the item that names it

To add a file, upload its bytes, then create an item that names the hash Marfa answers:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa blobs upload inventory.txt
```

```text
stored sha256:7fc0ba0d4e6818ccf1f3eae53ed1ce059625672ff5438d0ab59b12ab6e0305ef (64 bytes, text/plain)
```

</Terminal>

A file item is an item of `core.file` or a type beneath it, such as `core.file.image` for a photo. Its `blob_ref` is the hash, always `sha256:` and 64 hex digits:

```http title="Request"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.file",
  "properties": {
    "title": "Flat inventory",
    "blob_ref": "sha256:7fc0ba0d4e6818ccf1f3eae53ed1ce059625672ff5438d0ab59b12ab6e0305ef",
    "mime_type": "text/plain"
  }
}
```

Marfa sets `size_bytes` from the bytes it holds. [Upload and download files](/build/files-upload-download) walks through the rest.

## Find a file by what it says

**Marfa reads the text inside files,** such as a PDF's pages, and the text in images by OCR. It writes what it reads onto the item as `extracted_text`, and search matches it. An image also gains its `width` and `height`, and a recording its `duration`. Marfa does this for the file kinds and sizes it supports. Replacing the bytes clears a field the replacement doesn't set. The owner can turn text reading, or OCR alone, off in [Settings](/run/settings).

## Who may read a blob

**Knowing a hash isn't enough.** A credential reads a blob through an item it can read that names it: a file item, or an item with the hash in its text, such as an image in a note's body. A reference lends its read only if its writer had uploaded the bytes or could already read them, so a hash found somewhere grants nothing. A write that gives a file item a new `blob_ref` naming a hash its writer can't prove is refused `404 blob_not_found`.

A read of a blob no readable item names is `404 blob_not_found`, the answer for a blob you may not read and for one that doesn't exist, **even one you just uploaded.** Create the item straight after uploading: a blob no item names is purged at least a day after the upload, by default. A credential holding `blobs.manage` reads every blob.

A page or player that can't send a credential uses a **signed link**: `marfa blobs url` answers one that works without a credential, for an hour by default and up to seven days.

## How long a blob stays

A blob stays while something names it, including an item in the bin or an earlier version of an item. Once nothing does, a later [housekeeping](/run/housekeeping) run purges it, at least a day after it was found unnamed by default, and never while a backup Marfa keeps still names it. Every instance keeps its blobs on the disk beside the server, and can keep further copies, as [Back up and restore](/run/back-up-and-restore#use-an-object-store) explains.

The rules behind this page are in the [blobs](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/blobs.md) and [stores](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/stores.md) chapters of the contract.
